clause_path: Section 23 chapeau -- input_attestations entry shape and RFC 6901 pointer semantics

obligations.label: the hash proves what the artifact computed and nothing more; it is not evidence that the given inputs were genuine
the section adds a way for artifacts to carry outside vouching for named inputs on a per-input basis, and doing so leaves the meaning of the execution hash untouched
input evidence attaches at the optional top-level input_attestations array, which is attached after hashing and is excluded from execution_hash scope
conformance does not require any attestations at all; because they sit outside the preimage, attaching, dropping, or reordering them cannot alter a single byte of an existing hash
each attestation entry carries a type (one of vc-2.0, c2pa-manifest, rfc3161-snapshot, zktls), a pointer, a proof, and a source_ref
pointers are evaluated under RFC 6901 against the policy parameters alone rather than the whole artifact, and an entry whose pointer comes up empty is a structural failure that must be rejected
whatever node the pointer lands on is the attested value, and any digest a type binds for it has to be the SHA-256 of that node in canonical form
the vouching reference carries who is doing the attesting and informs the trust call, but it can never stand in for checking the proof itself
